# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

  2. For each stop in this.stops: add stop.stopStation to the list.
  3. Return the list.

Trip::calculateMonthlyPoints
Summary: Computes the total reward points earned by a customer from bookings on this trip in a given month.
Algorithm:
  1. If customer is null, return 0.
  2. If customer.membershipPackage is null or does not contain Award.POINTS, return 0.
  3. Initialize totalPoints = 0.
  4. For each booking in this.bookings:
     a. If booking.customer == customer and booking.isInMonth(currentMonth) is true, add (booking.numberOfSeats * 5) to totalPoints.
  5. Return totalPoints.
Related Features: bookings, price (unused here), departureTime (unused)
Related Classes: Booking, Customer, MembershipPackage, Award
Input: customer : Customer, currentMonth : String – format "yyyy-MM"
Output: int – total points (5 per seat per eligible booking)
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: No state change

Trip::isTimeConflicting
Summary: Checks if this trip's time interval overlaps with a given time interval.
Algorithm:
  1. Parse this.departureTime, this.arrivalTime, newDepartureTime, newArrivalTime as datetime strings.
  2. If invalid, return false.
  3. Overlap occurs if: this.departureTime < newArrivalTime AND newDepartureTime < this.arrivalTime.
  4. Adjacent boundaries (e.g., this.arrivalTime == newDepartureTime) are NOT considered overlapping.
  5. Return true if overlapping, false otherwise.
Related Features: departureTime, arrivalTime
Related Classes: None
Input: newDepartureTime : String, newArrivalTime : String – format "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"
Output: boolean – true if intervals overlap, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: No state change

Trip::bookSeats
Summary: Attempts to reserve the requested number of seats on this trip.
Algorithm:
  1. If num <= 0 or num > numberOfSeats, return false.
  2. Subtract num from numberOfSeats.
  3. Return true.
Related Features: numberOfSeats
Related Classes: None
Input: num : int – number of seats to book (must be positive)
Output: boolean – true if seats were successfully reserved, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If true, numberOfSeats is reduced by num.

Trip::calculateDiscountedPrice
Summary: Calculates the final price after applying a 20% discount if eligible.
Algorithm:
  1. If customer is null or bookingTime is null, return this.price.
  2. If customer.membershipPackage is null or does not contain Award.DISCOUNTS, return this.price.
  3. Calculate duration in hours between bookingTime and this.departureTime.
  4. If duration >= 24 hours, return Math.round(this.price * 0.8 * 10) / 10.0 (one decimal place).
  5. Otherwise, return this.price.
Related Features: price, departureTime, customer, customer.membershipPackage
Related Classes: Customer, MembershipPackage, Award
Input: customer : Customer, bookingTime : String – format "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"
Output: double – discounted or original price, rounded to one decimal place
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: No state change

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

  2. Let availableSeats = numberOfSeats - getBookedSeats().
  3. If num > availableSeats, return false.
  4. Subtract num from numberOfSeats.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: numberOfSeats, bookings
Related Classes: Booking
Input: num : int – number of seats to book (must be positive)
Output: boolean – true if seats were successfully reserved, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If true, numberOfSeats is reduced by num.

Trip::calculateDiscountedPrice
Summary: Calculates the final price after applying a 20% discount if eligible.
Algorithm:
  1. If customer is null or bookingTime is null, return this.price.
  2. If customer.membershipPackage is null or does not contain Award.DISCOUNTS, return this.price.
  3. Calculate duration in hours between bookingTime and this.departureTime.
  4. If duration >= 24 hours, return Math.round(this.price * 0.8 * 10) / 10.0 (one decimal place).
  5. Otherwise, return this.price.
Related Features: price, departureTime, customer, customer.membershipPackage
Related Classes: Customer, MembershipPackage, Award
Input: customer : Customer, bookingTime : String – format "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"
Output: double – discounted or original price, rounded to one decimal place
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: No state change

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Operation Specifications
Driver::checkStopOverlap
Summary: Determines whether two indirect trips share at least one common stop station (case-sensitive).
Algorithm:
  1. If trip1 is null or trip2 is null, return false.
  2. Get stop stations list from trip1.getStopStations() and trip2.getStopStations().
  3. If either list is empty, return false.
  4. For each station in trip1's list: if it exists in trip2's list (case-sensitive), return true.
  5. Return false.
Related Features: Trip.getStopStations()
Related Classes: Trip, Stop
Input: trip1 : Trip, trip2 : Trip
Output: boolean – true if they share at least one stop, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: No state change

Driver::canPostTrip
Summary: Validates whether a driver can publish a new trip based on time validity and no overlap with existing trips.
Algorithm:
  1. If newTrip is null, return false.
  2. If newTrip.departureTime or newTrip.arrivalTime is not a valid datetime in "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm", return false.
  3. If newTrip.departureTime is not strictly earlier than newTrip.arrivalTime, return false.
  4. For each existing trip in this.trips:
     a. If newTrip.isTimeConflicting(existingTrip.departureTime, existingTrip.arrivalTime) returns true, return false.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: trips, Trip.isTimeConflicting()
Related Classes: Trip
Input: newTrip : Trip – the proposed trip to publish
Output: boolean – true if the trip can be published, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: No state change (validation only)

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Operation Specifications
Customer::computeMonthlyRewardPoints
Summary: Computes total reward points earned by this customer for bookings in a given month.
Algorithm:
  1. If membershipPackage is null or does not contain Award.POINTS, return 0.
  2. Initialize totalPoints = 0.
  3. For each booking in this.bookings:
     a. If booking.isInMonth(currentMonth) is true, add (booking.numberOfSeats * 5) to totalPoints.
  4. Return totalPoints.
Related Features: bookings, membershipPackage, membershipPackage.hasAward()
Related Classes: Booking, MembershipPackage, Award
Input: currentMonth : String – format "yyyy-MM"
Output: int – total reward points (each seat contributes 5 points)
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: No state change

Customer::bookTrip
Summary: Attempts to create a booking for a given trip with the specified number of seats.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new Booking object with this customer, the given trip, numberOfSeats, and current date as bookingDate.
  2. Call newBooking.isBookingEligible().
  3. If eligible, add the new booking to this.bookings list and return true.
  4. Otherwise, discard the new booking and return false.
Related Features: bookings, MembershipPackage (indirectly via discount/points)
Related Classes: Booking, Trip
Input: trip : Trip, numberOfSeats : int
Output: boolean – true if booking was created successfully, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If true, a new Booking is added to this.bookings and the trip's seats are reduced.

The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.

# Operation Specifications
Customer::computeMonthlyRewardPoints
Summary: Computes total reward points earned by this customer for bookings in a given month.
Algorithm:
  1. If membershipPackage is null or does not contain Award.POINTS, return 0.
  2. Initialize totalPoints = 0.
  3. For each booking in this.bookings:
     a. If booking.isInMonth(currentMonth) is true, add (booking.numberOfSeats * 5) to totalPoints.
  4. Return totalPoints.
Related Features: bookings, membershipPackage, membershipPackage.hasAward()
Related Classes: Booking, MembershipPackage, Award
Input: currentMonth : String – format "yyyy-MM"
Output: int – total reward points (each seat contributes 5 points)
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: No state change

Customer::bookTrip
Summary: Attempts to create a booking for a given trip with the specified number of seats.
Algorithm:
  1. Create a new Booking object with this customer, the given trip, numberOfSeats, and current date as bookingDate.
  2. Call newBooking.isBookingEligible().
  3. If eligible, add the new booking to this.bookings list and return true.
  4. Otherwise, discard the new booking and return false.
Related Features: bookings, MembershipPackage (indirectly via discount/points)
Related Classes: Booking, Trip
Input: trip : Trip, numberOfSeats : int
Output: boolean – true if booking was created successfully, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If true, a new Booking is added to this.bookings and the trip's seats are reduced.

# Requirement
```text
Online Rideshare System (ORS) manages shared road trips between drivers and customers. Every user is identified by an id and also stores an email address and a phone number so that the platform can distinguish and contact the user.

A driver can publish trips. A trip records a departure station, an arrival station, the number of available seats, a departure date, a departure time, an arrival time, and a price. Trips can be direct or indirect. An indirect trip contains one or more stops, and each stop stores the name of its stop station.

A customer can create bookings for trips. A booking records the requested number of seats, the booking date, the related customer, and the related trip. A booking is valid only when the trip exists, enough seats are still available, the customer has no overlapping booking on the same day, and the booking is made more than two hours before the trip departure time. When a booking is accepted, the trip seat inventory must be reduced accordingly.

Customers may subscribe to a membership package. A membership package stores one or more rewards, and each reward is one of cashback, discounts, or points. A customer with a discount reward receives a 20 percent discount only when the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure. A customer with a points reward earns 5 points per booked seat for bookings created within the requested month.

A driver may publish a new trip only when the proposed trip has a valid time window and does not overlap with the driver’s existing trips. Two indirect trips posted by the same driver are considered overlapping by stops when they share at least one stop station, and stop-name comparison is case-sensitive.
Functional requirement:
1. Validate Booking Eligibility.
The system shall determine whether a customer can book seats on a trip. The trip must exist, the trip must still have enough available seats, the requested seats must not exceed the remaining seats, and the customer must not already hold another booking whose trip time overlaps on the same day. All time comparisons use the trip's `departureTime` and `arrivalTime` as datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`. The booking time must be strictly earlier than the departure time by more than two hours, so a booking made exactly two hours before departure is rejected. When the booking is accepted, the trip seat count shall be reduced. Invalid inputs such as a null customer, null trip, or null booking date shall return `false`.

2. Calculate Discounted Trip Price.
The system shall calculate the final price of a booking after reward evaluation. A fixed 20 percent discount applies only when the customer owns a membership package containing the `DISCOUNTS` award and the booking is made at least 24 hours before departure.Both bookingTime and the trip's departureTime are datetime strings in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm, and the 24-hour threshold is computed as the actual duration between the two datetimes (inclusive of the exact 24-hour boundary).The returned amount shall keep one decimal place. When the customer, membership package, booking time, or reward condition is invalid or missing, the original trip price shall be returned.

3. Check Stop Overlap for Indirect Trips.
The system shall determine whether two indirect trips posted by the same driver share at least one common stop station. The comparison is case-sensitive. If either trip is null or one of the stop collections is empty, the result shall be `false`.

4. Compute Monthly Reward Points.
The system shall compute the reward points earned by a customer during a given month. Only customers whose membership package contains the `POINTS` award are eligible. Only bookings whose booking date falls inside the requested month shall be counted. Each booked seat contributes 5 points. Invalid inputs, missing membership packages, or unsupported rewards shall return `0`.

5. Validate Trip Posting Feasibility.
The system shall validate whether a driver can publish a new trip. The proposed trip must exist, its departure time and arrival time must be valid datetime strings in the format `yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm`, and the departure time must be earlier than the arrival time. The new trip must not overlap with any existing trip of the driver, where time conflict is determined by comparing the full datetime intervals. Completely identical time periods are conflicts, while adjacent boundaries where one trip ends exactly when another starts are allowed. Invalid inputs shall return `false`.
```

# Operation Specifications
Booking::isInMonth
Summary: Checks if this booking's bookingDate falls within the specified month (format "yyyy-MM").
Algorithm:
  1. Parse bookingDate as EDate.
  2. Compare the year-month portion with the given month string.
  3. Return true if they match, false otherwise.
Related Features: bookingDate
Related Classes: None
Input: month : String – format "yyyy-MM", e.g., "2025-03"
Output: boolean – true if bookingDate is in that month, false otherwise
Pre-condition: month must be a valid string in "yyyy-MM" format
Post-condition: No state change

Booking::isBookingEligible
Summary: Determines whether a customer can book the specified number of seats on the associated trip.
Algorithm:
  1. If customer is null or trip is null or bookingDate is null, return false.
  2. If trip.bookSeats(numberOfSeats) returns false, return false.
  3. If this customer has any existing booking whose trip overlaps with this trip (using overlapsWith), return false.
  4. If bookingDate is not strictly more than 2 hours before trip.departureTime, return false.
  5. Return true.
Related Features: numberOfSeats, customer, trip, bookingDate, trip.bookSeats(), overlapsWith()
Related Classes: Customer, Trip, Booking
Input: None (uses internal fields: customer, trip, bookingDate, numberOfSeats)
Output: boolean – true if eligible, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: If true is returned, the trip's available seats have been reduced by numberOfSeats (via bookSeats). If false, no changes.

Booking::updateTripSeats
Summary: Reduces the number of available seats on the associated trip by the number of seats booked in this booking.
Algorithm:
  1. Call trip.bookSeats(this.numberOfSeats).
  2. Return nothing (void).
Related Features: numberOfSeats, trip, trip.bookSeats()
Related Classes: Trip
Input: None
Output: void
Pre-condition: trip must not be null
Post-condition: The trip's numberOfSeats is reduced by this.numberOfSeats (if enough seats remain).

Booking::overlapsWith
Summary: Checks if the time interval of this booking's trip overlaps with the time interval of another given trip.
Algorithm:
  1. If the other trip is null, return false.
  2. Compare the intervals [this.trip.departureTime, this.trip.arrivalTime] and [otherTrip.departureTime, otherTrip.arrivalTime].
  3. Overlap occurs if intervals intersect (including partial overlap, but not touching at exact boundaries).
  4. Return true if overlapping, false otherwise.
Related Features: trip, trip.departureTime, trip.arrivalTime
Related Classes: Trip
Input: trip : Trip – the other trip to compare
Output: boolean – true if time intervals overlap, false otherwise
Pre-condition: None
Post-condition: No state change

   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Validates whether a driver can publish a new trip based on time validity and no overlap with existing trips.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If newTrip is null, return false.
   *   2. If newTrip.departureTime or newTrip.arrivalTime is not a valid datetime in "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm", return false.
   *   3. If newTrip.departureTime is not strictly earlier than newTrip.arrivalTime, return false.
   *   4. For each existing trip in this.trips:
   *      a. If newTrip.isTimeConflicting(existingTrip.departureTime, existingTrip.arrivalTime) returns true, return false.
   *   5. Return true.
   * Related Features: trips, Trip.isTimeConflicting()
   * Related Classes: Trip
   * Input: newTrip : Trip – the proposed trip to publish
   * Output: boolean – true if the trip can be published, false otherwise
   * Pre-condition: None
   * Post-condition: No state change
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean canPostTrip(final Trip newtrip)
  {
    // 1. If newTrip is null, return false.
    if (newtrip == null)
    {
      return false;
    }
    // 2. If newTrip.departureTime or newTrip.arrivalTime is not a valid datetime in "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm", return false.
    String depTime = newtrip.getDepartureTime();
    String arrTime = newtrip.getArrivalTime();
    if (depTime == null || arrTime == null)
    {
      return false;
    }
    try
    {
      java.text.SimpleDateFormat sdf = new java.text.SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm");
      sdf.setLenient(false);
      sdf.parse(depTime);
      sdf.parse(arrTime);
    }
    catch (java.text.ParseException e)
    {
      return false;
    }
    // 3. If newTrip.departureTime is not strictly earlier than newTrip.arrivalTime, return false.
    try
    {
      java.text.SimpleDateFormat sdf = new java.text.SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm");
      java.util.Date depDate = sdf.parse(depTime);
      java.util.Date arrDate = sdf.parse(arrTime);
      if (!depDate.before(arrDate))
      {
        return false;
      }
    }
    catch (java.text.ParseException e)
    {
      return false;
    }
    // 4. For each existing trip in this.trips:
    for (Trip existingTrip : getTrips())
    {
      // a. If newTrip.isTimeConflicting(existingTrip.departureTime, existingTrip.arrivalTime) returns true, return false.
      if (newtrip.isTimeConflicting(existingTrip.getDepartureTime(), existingTrip.getArrivalTime()))
      {
        return false;
      }
    }
    // 5. Return true.
    return true;
  }

For `computeMonthlyRewardPoints`:

```java
public int computeMonthlyRewardPoints(final String currentMonth)
{
    if (membershipPackage == null || !membershipPackage.hasAward(Award.POINTS)) {
      return 0;
    }
    int totalPoints = 0;
    if (bookings != null) {
      for (Booking booking : bookings) {
        if (booking.isInMonth(currentMonth)) {
          totalPoints += booking.getNumberOfSeats() * 5;
        }
      }
    }
    return totalPoints;
}
```

For `bookTrip`:

```java
public void bookTrip(final Trip trip, final int numberOfSeats)
{
    if (trip == null || numberOfSeats <= 0) {
      return;
    }
    Booking newBooking = RideshareFactory.eINSTANCE.createBooking();
    newBooking.setCustomer(this);
    newBooking.setTrip(trip);
    newBooking.setNumberOfSeats(numberOfSeats);
    newBooking.setBookingDate(new java.util.Date());
    
    if (newBooking.isBookingEligible()) {
      getBookings().add(newBooking);
      newBooking.updateTripSeats();
    }
}
```

```java
public int computeMonthlyRewardPoints(final String currentMonth)
{
```
```java
    if (membershipPackage == null || !membershipPackage.hasAward(Award.POINTS)) {
      return 0;
    }
    int totalPoints = 0;
    if (bookings != null) {
      for (Booking booking : bookings) {
        if (booking.isInMonth(currentMonth)) {
          totalPoints += booking.getNumberOfSeats() * 5;
        }
      }
    }
    return totalPoints;
}
```

For `bookTrip`:

```java
public void bookTrip(final Trip trip, final int numberOfSeats)
{
    if (trip == null || numberOfSeats <= 0) {
      return;
    }
    Booking newBooking = RideshareFactory.eINSTANCE.createBooking();
    newBooking.setCustomer(this);
    newBooking.setTrip(trip);
    newBooking.setNumberOfSeats(numberOfSeats);
    newBooking.setBookingDate(new java.util.Date());
    
    if (newBooking.isBookingEligible()) {
      getBookings().add(newBooking);
      newBooking.updateTripSeats();
    }
}
```

```java
    }
```

```java
    if (membershipPackage == null) {
```

    }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Calculates the final price of a booking after reward evaluation.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If customer is null or bookingTime is null, return this.price.
   *   2. Get customer's membershipPackage. If null, return this.price.
   *   3. If membershipPackage does not have DISCOUNTS award, return this.price.
   *   4. Parse bookingTime and this.departureTime as datetime strings (format "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm").
   *   5. If bookingTime is at least 24 hours before departureTime, return price * 0.8 rounded to 1 decimal place.
   *   6. Otherwise, return this.price.
   * Related Features: price, departureTime, customer, membershipPackage
   * Related Classes: Customer, MembershipPackage, Award
   * Input: customer : Customer, bookingTime : String – format "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"
   * Output: double – the discounted price (1 decimal place) or original price
   * Pre-condition: None
   * Post-condition: No state change
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public double calculateDiscountedPrice(final Customer customer, final String bookingTime)
  {
    if (customer == null || bookingTime == null) {
      return this.price;
    }
    MembershipPackage membershipPackage = customer.getMembershipPackage();
    if (membershipPackage == null) {
      return this.price;
    }
    if (!membershipPackage.hasAward(Award.DISCOUNTS)) {
      return this.price;
    }
    SimpleDateFormat sdf = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm");
    try {
      Date bookingDateTime = sdf.parse(bookingTime);
      Date departureDateTime = sdf.parse(this.departureTime);
      long diff = departureDateTime.getTime() - bookingDateTime.getTime();
      if (diff >= 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000L) {
        double discountedPrice = this.price * 0.8;
        return Math.round(discountedPrice * 10) / 10.0;
      }
    } catch (ParseException e) {
      return this.price;
    }
    return this.price;
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Computes the reward points earned by a customer during a given month.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If customer is null or currentMonth is null, return 0.
   *   2. Get customer's membershipPackage. If null, return 0.
   *   3. If membershipPackage does not have POINTS award, return 0.
   *   4. Initialize totalPoints = 0.
   *   5. For each booking in customer.bookings:
   *      a. If booking.isInMonth(currentMonth) returns true, add booking.numberOfSeats * 5 to totalPoints.
   *   6. Return totalPoints.
   * Related Features: customer, bookings, numberOfSeats, isInMonth()
   * Related Classes: Customer, Booking, MembershipPackage, Award
   * Input: customer : Customer, currentMonth : String – format "yyyy-MM"
   * Output: int – total reward points earned
   * Pre-condition: None
   * Post-condition: No state change
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public int calculateMonthlyPoints(final Customer customer, final String currentMonth)
  {
    if (customer == null || currentMonth == null) {
      return 0;
    }
    MembershipPackage membershipPackage = customer.getMembershipPackage();
    if (membershipPackage == null) {
      return 0;
    }
    if (!membershipPackage.hasAward(Award.POINTS)) {
      return 0;
    }
    int totalPoints = 0;
    for (Booking booking : customer.getBookings()) {
      if (booking.isInMonth(currentMonth)) {
        totalPoints += booking.getNumberOfSeats() * 5;
      }
    }
    return totalPoints;
  }

   * Summary: Attempts to reserve the requested number of seats on this trip.

   *   1. If num <= 0, return false.
   *   2. Let availableSeats = numberOfSeats - getBookedSeats().

   * Related Classes: Booking
   * Input: num : int – number of seats to book (must be positive)
   * Output: boolean – true if seats were successfully reserved, false otherwise
   * Pre-condition: None
   * Post-condition: If true, numberOfSeats is reduced by num.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean bookSeats(final int num)
  {
    if (num <= 0) {
      return false;
    }
    int availableSeats = numberOfSeats - getBookedSeats();
    if (num > availableSeats) {
      return false;
    }
    setNumberOfSeats(numberOfSeats - num);
    return true;
  }

  /**
   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->
   * <!-- end-user-doc -->
   * <!-- begin-model-doc -->
   * Summary: Checks if the proposed trip's time interval conflicts with this trip's time interval.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If newDepartureTime is null or newArrivalTime is null, return false.
   *   2. Parse newDepartureTime and newArrivalTime as datetime strings (format "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm").
   *   3. If newDepartureTime >= newArrivalTime, return false.
   *   4. Compare intervals [this.departureTime, this.arrivalTime] and [newDepartureTime, newArrivalTime].
   *   5. Overlap occurs if intervals intersect (excluding exact boundary adjacency).
   *   6. Return true if overlapping, false otherwise.
   * Related Features: departureTime, arrivalTime
   * Related Classes: None
   * Input: newDepartureTime : String, newArrivalTime : String – format "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"
   * Output: boolean – true if time intervals conflict, false otherwise
   * Pre-condition: None
   * Post-condition: No state change
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean isTimeConflicting(final String newDepartureTime, final String newArrivalTime)
  {
    if (newDepartureTime == null || newArrivalTime == null) {
      return false;
    }
    SimpleDateFormat sdf = new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm");
    try {
      Date newDepart = sdf.parse(newDepartureTime);
      Date newArrive = sdf.parse(newArrivalTime);
      if (newDepart.getTime() >= newArrive.getTime()) {
        return false;
      }
      Date thisDepart = sdf.parse(this.departureTime);
      Date thisArrive = sdf.parse(this.arrivalTime);
      return thisDepart.getTime() < newArrive.getTime() && newDepart.getTime() < thisArrive.getTime();
    } catch (ParseException e) {
      return false;
    }
  }

```java
   * Summary: Determines whether a customer can book the specified number of seats on the associated trip.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If customer is null or trip is null or bookingDate is null, return false.
   *   2. If trip.getAvailableSeats() < numberOfSeats, return false.
   *   3. If this customer has any existing booking whose trip overlaps with this trip (using overlapsWith), return false.
   *   4. If the current time is not strictly more than 2 hours before trip.departureTime, return false.
   *   5. Return true.
   * Related Features: numberOfSeats, customer, trip, bookingDate, trip.getAvailableSeats(), overlapsWith()
   * Related Classes: Customer, Trip, Booking
   * Input: None (uses internal fields: customer, trip, bookingDate, numberOfSeats)
   * Output: boolean – true if eligible, false otherwise
   * Pre-condition: None
   * Post-condition: If true is returned, the trip's available seats have been reduced by numberOfSeats. If false, no changes.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model kind="operation"
   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
```
```java
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean isBookingEligible()
  {
    // 1. If customer is null or trip is null or bookingDate is null, return false.
    if (getCustomer() == null || getTrip() == null || getBookingDate() == null) {
      return false;
    }
    
    // 2. If trip.getAvailableSeats() < numberOfSeats, return false.
    int availableSeats = getTrip().getNumberOfSeats() - getTrip().getBookedSeats();
    if (availableSeats < getNumberOfSeats()) {
      return false;
    }
    
    // 3. If this customer has any existing booking whose trip overlaps with this trip (using overlapsWith), return false.
    for (Booking existingBooking : getCustomer().getBookings()) {
      if (existingBooking != this && existingBooking.overlapsWith(getTrip())) {
        return false;
      }
    }
    
    // 4. If the current time is not strictly more than 2 hours before trip.departureTime, return false.
    try {
      java.text.SimpleDateFormat sdf = new java.text.SimpleDateFormat("HH:mm");
      java.util.Date currentTime = new java.util.Date();
      java.util.Date departureTime = sdf.parse(getTrip().getDepartureTime());
      
      // Create a calendar for current time to get just the time portion
      java.util.Calendar cal = java.util.Calendar.getInstance();
      cal.setTime(currentTime);
      int currentHour = cal.get(java.util.Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY);
      int currentMinute = cal.get(java.util.Calendar.MINUTE);
      String currentTimeStr = String.format("%02d:%02d", currentHour, currentMinute);
      java.util.Date currentTimeOnly = sdf.parse(currentTimeStr);
      
      // Check if current time is strictly more than 2 hours before departure
      long diffMillis = departureTime.getTime() - currentTimeOnly.getTime();
      long twoHoursMillis = 2 * 60 * 60 * 1000L;
      if (diffMillis <= twoHoursMillis) {
        return false;
      }
    } catch (Exception e) {
      return false;
    }
    
    // 5. Return true.
    return true;

   * Input: trip : Trip – the other trip to compare
   * Output: boolean – true if time intervals overlap, false otherwise

   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean overlapsWith(final Trip trip)
  {
    // 1. If the other trip is null, return false.
    if (trip == null) {
      return false;
    }
    
    // 2. Compare the intervals [this.trip.departureTime, this.trip.arrivalTime] and [otherTrip.departureTime, otherTrip.arrivalTime].
    try {
      java.text.SimpleDateFormat sdf = new java.text.SimpleDateFormat("HH:mm");
      
      java.util.Date thisDeparture = sdf.parse(getTrip().getDepartureTime());
      java.util.Date thisArrival = sdf.parse(getTrip().getArrivalTime());
      java.util.Date otherDeparture = sdf.parse(trip.getDepartureTime());
      java.util.Date otherArrival = sdf.parse(trip.getArrivalTime());
      
      // 3. Overlap occurs if intervals intersect (including partial overlap and exact boundaries).
      // Two intervals [a1, a2] and [b1, b2] overlap if a1 <= b2 AND b1 <= a2
      if (thisDeparture.compareTo(otherArrival) <= 0 && otherDeparture.compareTo(thisArrival) <= 0) {
        return true;
      }
    } catch (Exception e) {
      return false;
    }
    
    // 4. Return true if overlapping, false otherwise.
    return false;
  }

    String bookingYearMonth = sdf.format(getBookingDate());
    
    // 3. Return true if they match, false otherwise.
    return bookingYearMonth.equals(month);
  }
```

```java
    try {

      java.util.Date thisArrival = sdf.parse(getTrip().getArrivalTime());
```

   * Summary: Determines whether a customer can book the specified number of seats on the associated trip.
   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If customer is null or trip is null or bookingDate is null, return false.
   *   2. If trip.getAvailableSeats() < numberOfSeats, return false.
   *   3. If this customer has any existing booking whose trip overlaps with this trip (using overlapsWith), return false.
   *   4. If the current time is not strictly more than 2 hours before trip.departureTime, return false.
   *   5. Return true.
   * Related Features: numberOfSeats, customer, trip, bookingDate, trip.getAvailableSeats(), overlapsWith()
   * Related Classes: Customer, Trip, Booking
   * Input: None (uses internal fields: customer, trip, bookingDate, numberOfSeats)
   * Output: boolean – true if eligible, false otherwise
   * Pre-condition: None
   * Post-condition: If true is returned, the trip's available seats have been reduced by numberOfSeats. If false, no changes.
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model kind="operation"
   *        annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean isBookingEligible()
  {
    // 1. If customer is null or trip is null or bookingDate is null, return false.
    if (getCustomer() == null || getTrip() == null || getBookingDate() == null) {
      return false;
    }
    // 2. If trip.getAvailableSeats() < numberOfSeats, return false.
    int availableSeats = getTrip().getNumberOfSeats() - getTrip().getBookedSeats();
    if (availableSeats < getNumberOfSeats()) {
      return false;
    }
    // 3. If this customer has any existing booking whose trip overlaps with this trip (using overlapsWith), return false.
    for (Booking existingBooking : getCustomer().getBookings()) {
      if (existingBooking != this && existingBooking.overlapsWith(getTrip())) {
        return false;
      }
    }
    // 4. If the current time is not strictly more than 2 hours before trip.departureTime, return false.
    try {
      java.text.SimpleDateFormat sdf = new java.text.SimpleDateFormat("HH:mm");
      java.util.Calendar cal = java.util.Calendar.getInstance();
      String currentTimeStr = String.format("%02d:%02d", cal.get(java.util.Calendar.HOUR_OF_DAY), cal.get(java.util.Calendar.MINUTE));
      java.util.Date currentTimeOnly = sdf.parse(currentTimeStr);
      java.util.Date departureTime = sdf.parse(getTrip().getDepartureTime());
      long diffMillis = departureTime.getTime() - currentTimeOnly.getTime();
      long twoHoursMillis = 2L * 60 * 60 * 1000;
      if (diffMillis <= twoHoursMillis) {
        return false;
      }
    } catch (Exception e) {
      return false;
    }
    // 5. Return true.
    return true;
  }

   * <!-- begin-user-doc -->

   * Algorithm:
   *   1. If the other trip is null, return false.
   *   2. Compare the intervals [this.trip.departureTime, this.trip.arrivalTime] and [otherTrip.departureTime, otherTrip.arrivalTime].
   *   3. Overlap occurs if intervals intersect (including partial overlap and exact boundaries).
   *   4. Return true if overlapping, false otherwise.
   * Related Features: trip, trip.departureTime, trip.arrivalTime
   * Related Classes: Trip
   * Input: trip : Trip – the other trip to compare
   * Output: boolean – true if time intervals overlap, false otherwise
   * Pre-condition: None
   * Post-condition: No state change
   * <!-- end-model-doc -->
   * @model annotation="http://www.ustb.edu.cn/sei/mde/EnhancedCodeGen generated='true'"
   * @generated NOT
   */
  public boolean overlapsWith(final Trip trip)
  {
    // 1. If the other trip is null, return false.
    if (trip == null) {
      return false;
    }
    // 2. Compare the intervals [this.trip.departureTime, this.trip.arrivalTime] and [otherTrip.departureTime, otherTrip.arrivalTime].
    try {
      java.text.SimpleDateFormat sdf = new java.text.SimpleDateFormat("HH:mm");
      java.util.Date thisDeparture = sdf.parse(getTrip().getDepartureTime());
      java.util.Date thisArrival = sdf.parse(getTrip().getArrivalTime());
      java.util.Date otherDeparture = sdf.parse(trip.getDepartureTime());
      java.util.Date otherArrival = sdf.parse(trip.getArrivalTime());
      // 3. Overlap occurs if intervals intersect (including partial overlap and exact boundaries).
      if (thisDeparture.compareTo(otherArrival) <= 0 && otherDeparture.compareTo(thisArrival) <= 0) {
        return true;
      }
    } catch (Exception e) {
      return false;
    }
    // 4. Return true if overlapping, false otherwise.
    return false;
  }

    String bookingYearMonth = sdf.format(getBookingDate());
    // 3. Return true if they match, false otherwise.
